articles.title: Apple's iPhone Duo Is Here: Dos and Don'ts for Your First Folding Phone
articles.excerpt: Apple's first folding phone reaches stores on Friday at $1,999. The Associated Press's One Tech Tip collects the care rules that apply to the Duo and every foldable: nothing between the screens, no backward bends, and keep it away from keys, coins and crumbs.
articles.image_caption: A book-style folding phone stands half-open, showing the hinge and inner display. Apple's iPhone Duo, its first foldable, reaches stores on Friday priced from $1,999.
articles.nri_angle: At $1,999, the Duo is the most expensive iPhone ever; the care steps in the how-to card are the difference between a two-year phone and a cracked inner display.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Never bend it backward or force it
steps.detail: Do not bend the phone backward, and do not use excessive force when opening or closing it — the AP's core rule for the Duo and every foldable.
Make sure nothing sits between the screens — no card, coin or key — which Samsung warns can scratch or puncture the main screen.

steps.step: Keep it away from crumbs and sharp objects
steps.detail: Google advises avoiding contact with crumbs, fingernails and sharp objects on the inner display.
Foldables have strong magnets along their edges that attract metal; several makers recommend not carrying the phone with keys or coins.

steps.step: Mind the cold, and don't store it shut for weeks
steps.detail: Honor advises against opening or closing its foldables in extreme cold, when screens can turn brittle, and against leaving a phone closed for long periods, which stresses the hinge.

steps.step: Clean it like a normal phone
steps.detail: Follow standard smartphone cleaning and maintenance practices to help the device last.
